scope: Independent read-only source, frozen patch, metadata and retained observation review. Only this report is written; no Cargo, Rust compilation, native test, Python test suite, control probe, source edit, GitHub or external action is performed by this reviewer.

verdict.recommendation: Worth incorporating as a narrowly scoped future-observation improvement, subject to exact candidate source compilation/lints/native controls and unchanged resource budgets. It exposes actual legacy dispatch messages without granting them typed identity. It does not close historical attribution, source-specific native execution or service-performance acceptance.

findings.v1_problem: The v1 reader validated code syntax and kind membership independently and would accept typed ROOT, typed PUBLIC_EOF with cancelled kind, or REMOTE_TERMINAL with transport kind. This was established by reading its predicate, not by running a new probe.
findings.v2_resolution: Reject typed ROOT and all non-null typed codes with unclassified kind; remote_refusal permits only no code or REMOTE_TERMINAL/REMOTE_RETRYABLE; those controlled remote codes permit remote_refusal/local_structure; PUBLIC_EOF permits transport/local_structure. Validation never derives code or origin from Display text.
findings.limit: This deliberately narrow set of relations is not a complete ErrorCode-to-ErrorKind registry. Unknown uppercase code spellings with otherwise allowed kinds are not universally rejected. Neither text nor ErrorKind authenticates control origin.

findings.finding: Capture adds no new heap-allocation call or lock acquisition, but optional observer records become materially larger and formatting/copying/serialization have nonzero cost. Existing optional try_lock scopes become longer by bounded capture work.
findings.action: Measure size_of/deltas and observed memory under the original profile before making a resource-cost claim; do not raise capacity or Host limits to hide the overhead.

findings.finding: Original source-116 F0 has 406 request records, 295 rejected dispatches with typed code null, and no new attachments. 294 have terminal response/null and one has work/PUBLIC_EOF. These facts cannot identify all 295 as ROOT or establish their causal relation to EOF.
findings.action: Retain all original nulls and source binding. Only future actual captures may carry new diagnostic text.

findings.finding: The two Rust candidate files have not been compiled or executed in this review. b280 native results and the final current-ELF registry belong to a different source/ELF and cannot be promoted into candidate results.
findings.action: After adoption, build the exact combined source under the original profile and execute the existing observer/error/paid-TCP ROOT controls plus the added meaningful controls. Preserve original assertions, registry entries, ignored tests, deadlines and resource budgets.

control_and_boundary_review.check: Original nineteen stages, acceptance, cancellation, deadline and cache boundaries
evidence: Five source regions are byte-identical and separately fingerprinted below.

control_and_boundary_review.check: Display text remains independent of typed identity
evidence: error.rs:503 display_changes_cannot_change_typed_retry_or_owner_stop_identity keeps typed code/kind authority independent from prose
error.rs:273-275 local_integrity can override kind to local_structure while retaining code
error.rs:339-359 distinguishes untyped remote text from controlled RemoteTerminal/RemoteRetryable
v2 reader controls preserve changed Display including ROOT while retaining the independently supplied typed code
control_and_boundary_review.withdrawn_initial_suggestion: Requiring Display to equal a typed code, or deriving EOF/ROOT origin from text, would violate existing semantics and was explicitly withdrawn.

evidence: ObservedErrorDiagnostic has a private 96-byte fixed buffer, private length and truncation state.
write_str takes min(input byte length, remaining capacity), backs up only to a UTF-8 boundary, copies only that prefix, then refuses further text once truncated.
Because input is str, boundary retreat is at most three bytes; length remains <=96 and no full-message scan is introduced.
Error Display at error.rs:375-378 is only f.write_str(&self.message), not recursive source formatting or allocation.
Serialization reads only bytes[..len], and no Error/source object is retained in the new data.
control_and_boundary_review.limit: The 96-byte limit is decoded UTF-8 message bytes. JSON escaping can expand those bytes (up to six output bytes for an ASCII control character), so it is not a 96-byte serialized-object limit. This is bounded raw diagnostic retention, not text sanitization or origin authentication.

control_and_boundary_review.check: No added wait or capture allocation
evidence: Existing Handle::update and update_task remain byte-identical and use try_lock.
Capture occurs inside the already successful try_lock callback, not before acquisition or in a blocking retry.
write! targets the fixed writer; it does not construct a String, Vec, Box or source chain.

Snapshot retains the existing blocking lock behavior. coverage_complete is intended after service/worker joins; a live snapshot is not atomic. No new snapshot lock is added or turned into an authorization or timing exemption.
control_and_boundary_review.limit: The existing Arc<Cell> allocation is larger and snapshots/output carry larger data. Lock hold duration and measured cost are not zero.

evidence: public_v3.rs:1839 passes observer=None for default metrics service
public_v3.rs:2264-2266 does not call connection() with None
public_v3.rs:2689-2692 does not create TaskObservation when no connection observation exists
public_v3.rs:2173-2175 and 2785-2786 only call diagnostic methods when records exist
TaskObservation::local sets network=None; update_task does not run the capture closure
control_and_boundary_review.conclusion: With no request observer, no new Cell/diagnostic field construction or clearing, message formatting, added diagnostic allocation or added diagnostic lock is executed. This is a source-path conclusion, not a measured zero-cycle or identical-binary claim.

control_and_boundary_review.check: Reader version, shape, bounds and association
evidence: Exact attachment schema, six top-level keys, three detail keys, no-control-authority=false and untrusted=true flags, integer byte capacity exactly96
Known ErrorKind spelling, string message and exact boolean truncation; UTF-8 size<=96 and truncated prefix>=93
Typed slots must exist; a missing detail cannot accompany known typed cause; an accepted dispatch cannot carry Err detail; terminal Err must have a string phase
v2 rejects the specific impossible code/kind combinations in ED-01 and preserves local_integrity exceptions
Dispatch and terminal summaries remain separate; neither infers that ROOT caused EOF nor that EOF is the dispatch cause
Attachments require v4 observer scope; a missing historical attachment returns without synthesizing data
limits: No complete ErrorCode policy table is duplicated.
No global inference of private budget origin or requires_owner_stop is made.
The terminal phase is checked as a string, not authenticated as a causal producer.
This reader is local evidence-consistency checking, not Host authentication, consensus or release acceptance.

memory_estimate.target_assumption: x86_64, 8-byte pointer/usize alignment, typical rustc niche layout; Rust repr(Rust) aggregate layout is not guaranteed and these are estimates, not measured bounds.
memory_estimate.allocation_timing: Cells are allocated only for retained accepted connections, up to observer capacity; they retain space even when diagnostics are None. Creating an observer preallocates its unchanged slot registry. None initialization does not guarantee that Rust clears all inactive payload bytes; actual capture explicitly clears its 96-byte buffer.
not_included: existing row padding or layout reordering
serialized JSON output and Python objects
cache effects and elapsed CPU/wall cost
minimal_followup_measurement: base/candidate size_of::<PublicRequestObservation>() and TaskProgress and Cell
original-profile observed memory/CPU with and without observer; no budget relaxation

smaller_reliable_options.option: Keep v2 as the generic two-boundary attachment
smaller_reliable_options.assessment: Recommended if both dispatch and terminal legacy causes are required. The separate slots preserve an actual dispatch ROOT together with later EOF/cancellation without reclassification; one combined error slot would lose that distinction.

A smaller scope can address the specific 295 untyped-dispatch observation gap while retaining the original terminal typed code. It would deliberately leave legacy terminal text unknown and needs a clear schema. This is a scope tradeoff, not required for safety; no edit is proposed in this review.

smaller_reliable_options.option: Compact internal fields after actual size measurement
smaller_reliable_options.assessment: If original memory budget is materially affected, a u8 length and compact stored kind with string mapping only during serialization, plus constant metadata emitted at serialization, can reduce redundant bytes. Do not start a broad Cell/storage refactor or add per-error allocation before measurement.

smaller_reliable_options.option: Promote ROOT text into ErrorCode or route through a formatted logger
smaller_reliable_options.assessment: Rejected. It changes semantic/control identity or adds logging/formatting/locking cost and does not preserve the explicit original Error boundary.

completion_limits: This is a read-only candidate review, not adoption approval, native PASS or performance qualification.
No existing deadline, Host budget, capacity, cache boundary or test expectation is relaxed.
Future candidate source and ELF require their own evidence; previous b280/116 measurements retain their original identity.
